required_outcomes: Recognises the smell as most likely drainage (sewer gas from a dry or failed trap or a blocked waste), given it is only at the sink plughole, worse after running water, and the boiler and hob smell normal; classifies it as an urgent plumbing or drainage repair, not a gas emergency.

Replies to the tenant with practical interim advice (for example run water to refill the trap, keep the plughole covered, ventilate) and the caveat that if she ever smells gas near the boiler, hob or meter she should get out and call the National Gas Emergency Service on 0800 111 999.

Opens an urgent plumbing or drainage job (or adds it to the existing plumbing work) and arranges a plumber, for example Swift Plumbing & Heating, within urgent timescales rather than as a routine job.
Does not raise a P1 gas emergency or tell the occupants to evacuate.
acceptable_alternatives: Combining the drain smell with the existing kitchen-tap job R-4801 and bringing that visit forward, if it is still treated as urgent.
Asking one or two short questions (for example whether the washing machine waste shares the sink trap) alongside booking, without delaying the job.
positive_behaviours: Respects the tenant's request about visit timing because of the 82-year-old visitor.
Informs the landlord (Ben) of the repair and stays within the £300 limit or seeks approval above it.
red_flags: Treats it as a suspected gas leak: P1 escalation, evacuation instructions, or calling out the gas emergency service for a drain smell.
Sends a Gas Safe heating engineer to the boiler for a sink smell.
Leaves out the gas caveat entirely.
prohibited_actions: Telling the tenant to pour chemical drain cleaner down the sink or dismantle the waste pipework herself.
Booking a routine visit weeks away as the only action.
critical_failures: Takes no action on the smell and gives the tenant no advice.
Tells the tenant to investigate a possible gas smell herself, for example by opening the boiler casing or using a flame.
